question: In an air brake system, at approximately what pressure does the governor stop the air compressor from pumping air (the "cut-out" pressure)?
explanation: The manual states that when air tank pressure rises to the "cut-out" level, around 125 psi, the governor stops the compressor from pumping air.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1 - The Parts of an Air Brake System (Governor)

question: At approximately what pressure does the governor allow the air compressor to start pumping air again (the "cut-in" pressure)?
explanation: The manual states that when tank pressure falls to the "cut-in" pressure, around 100 psi, the governor allows the compressor to start pumping again.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1 - The Parts of an Air Brake System (Governor)

question: What is the purpose of the air storage tanks (reservoirs) in an air brake system?
choice_a: To cool the compressed air before it reaches the brakes
choice_b: To filter oil out of the compressed air
choice_c: To hold compressed air so the brakes can be used several times even if the compressor stops working
choice_d: To power the spring brakes directly without any air pressure
explanation: The manual explains that air storage tanks hold enough compressed air to allow the brakes to be used several times, even if the compressor stops working.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.3 - Air Storage Tanks

question: According to the manual, what are the two types of air tank drain valves?
explanation: Each air tank has a drain valve in the bottom, and the manual describes two types: manually operated (quarter turn or cable) and automatic.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.4 - Air Tank Drains

topic: Why air tanks must be drained
question: Why is it important to drain air tanks completely?
choice_a: Because compressed air normally contains water and compressor oil that collect in the tank and can freeze or damage the system
choice_b: To increase the governor cut-out pressure
choice_d: To test whether the governor is working
explanation: Compressed air usually has water and compressor oil in it, which collect in the bottom of the tank; the water can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure if not drained.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.4 - Air Tank Drains

question: How is a manually operated air tank drain valve typically operated?
choice_a: By pressing a button on the dashboard
choice_b: By turning it a quarter turn or by pulling a cable
choice_c: By opening it with a wrench on the brake chamber
choice_d: By twisting the supply pressure gauge
explanation: The manual states manually operated drain valves are operated by turning a quarter turn or by pulling a cable, and must be drained at the end of each day of driving.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.4 - Air Tank Drains

question: What feature is available on automatic air tanks to help prevent freezing of the automatic drain in cold weather?
choice_a: An alcohol evaporator built into the drain
explanation: The manual notes that automatic air tanks are available with electric heating devices, which help prevent freezing of the automatic drain in cold weather.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.4 - Air Tank Drains

question: What is the purpose of an alcohol evaporator in an air brake system?
choice_a: To clean oil out of the air tank
choice_b: To increase the compressor's cut-out pressure
choice_d: To put alcohol into the air system to help reduce the risk of ice forming in air brake valves and other parts in cold weather
explanation: The manual states some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator to put alcohol into the air system, reducing the risk of ice in air brake valves during cold weather.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.5 - Alcohol Evaporator

question: According to the manual, how often should you check the alcohol container and fill it as necessary during cold weather?
choice_d: Only before the first snow of the season
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to check the alcohol container and fill up as necessary every day during cold weather, noting daily air tank drainage is still needed unless the system has automatic drain valves.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.5 - Alcohol Evaporator

question: The safety relief valve installed in the first tank an air compressor pumps air to is usually set to open at what pressure?
explanation: The manual states the safety valve is usually set to open at 150 psi to protect the tank and system from too much pressure.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.6 - Safety Valve

question: Where is the safety relief valve installed in an air brake system?
choice_a: In the brake chamber at each wheel
choice_c: In the first tank the air compressor pumps air to
choice_d: In the application pressure gauge line
explanation: According to the manual, a safety relief valve is installed in the first tank the air compressor pumps air to, protecting the tank and rest of the system from too much pressure.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.6 - Safety Valve

question: Besides "brake pedal," what is this control also called according to the manual?
choice_a: The master cylinder or slack valve
choice_d: The foot valve or treadle valve
explanation: The manual states the brake pedal is also called the foot valve or treadle valve.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.7 - The Brake Pedal

question: What can happen if you press and release the brake pedal unnecessarily?
choice_a: Air can be released faster than the compressor can replace it, and if pressure gets too low the brakes won't work
choice_b: The safety valve will permanently open at 150 psi
choice_c: The spring brakes will lock on permanently
choice_d: The wig wag will rise out of view permanently
explanation: The manual warns that pressing and releasing the pedal unnecessarily can let air out faster than the compressor can replace it, and if pressure gets too low, the brakes won't work.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.7 - The Brake Pedal

question: What is the most common type of foundation brake used at each wheel?
explanation: The manual states foundation brakes are used at each wheel and the most common type is the s-cam drum brake.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.8 - Foundation Brakes

question: In an s-cam brake, what happens when the brake pedal is pushed?
choice_a: A power screw clamps the disc between brake lining pads like a c-clamp
choice_b: A wedge is pushed directly between the ends of two brake shoes
choice_c: The s-cam forces the brake shoes away from one another and presses them against the inside of the brake drum
choice_d: The front brake limiting valve cuts pressure to the front axle by half
explanation: The manual explains that air pressure turns the camshaft, which rotates the s-cam, forcing the brake shoes apart and pressing them against the inside of the brake drum.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.8 - Foundation Brakes (S-cam Brakes)

question: How does a wedge brake apply the brake shoes against the drum?
choice_a: An s-cam twists to spread the shoes apart
choice_b: A power screw clamps a rotor between caliper pads
choice_c: A diaphragm pushes a piston against a disc
choice_d: The brake chamber push rod pushes a wedge directly between the ends of two brake shoes, shoving them apart against the drum
explanation: The manual describes wedge brakes as using the brake chamber push rod to push a wedge between the ends of two brake shoes, shoving them apart and against the inside of the brake drum.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.8 - Foundation Brakes (Wedge Brakes)

question: In air-operated disc brakes, what part turns to clamp the disc (rotor) between the brake lining pads of a caliper?
explanation: The manual states that instead of an s-cam, air-operated disc brakes use a power screw, turned by the slack adjuster, which clamps the disc between the caliper's brake lining pads similar to a large c-clamp.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.8 - Foundation Brakes (Disc Brakes)

question: In a vehicle with a dual air brake system, how is air tank pressure typically displayed to the driver?
choice_a: With one combined gauge showing a single average value
choice_b: With a gauge for each half of the system, or a single gauge with two needles
choice_c: With a warning buzzer only and no gauge
choice_d: Only on the application pressure gauge
explanation: The manual states that if the vehicle has a dual air brake system, there will be a gauge for each half of the system, or a single gauge with two needles.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.9 - Supply Pressure Gauges

question: According to the manual, what does it mean if you find yourself increasing application pressure to hold the same speed?
choice_a: The governor is cutting out early
choice_b: The spring brakes are beginning to engage
explanation: The manual explains that increasing application pressure to hold the same speed means the brakes are fading, and you should slow down and use a lower gear.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.10 - Application Pressure Gauge

question: A low air pressure warning signal you can see must come on before the air pressure in the tanks falls below what level?
explanation: The manual states a warning signal you can see must come on before air pressure in the tanks falls below 60 psi (or one half the compressor governor cutout pressure on older vehicles).
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.11 - Low Air Pressure Warning

topic: Low air pressure warning signal type
question: What is the low air pressure warning signal usually, according to the manual?
choice_a: A red light, and a buzzer may also come on
choice_c: Only a mechanical arm, with no light or buzzer
explanation: The manual states the warning is usually a red light, and a buzzer may also come on.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.11 - Low Air Pressure Warning

question: What is the "wig wag" low air pressure warning device?
choice_a: An electronic message displayed on the dashboard
choice_b: A mechanical arm that drops into the driver's view when system pressure drops below 60 psi
choice_c: A horn that sounds continuously until the engine is shut off
choice_d: A valve that automatically closes off air to the front brakes
explanation: The manual describes the wig wag as a device that drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when pressure drops below 60 psi, and rises out of view (if automatic) when pressure rises above 60 psi.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.11 - Low Air Pressure Warning

topic: Low pressure warning on large buses
question: On large buses, it is common for the low pressure warning devices to signal at what pressure range?
explanation: The manual notes that on large buses it is common for the low pressure warning devices to signal at 80-85 psi.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.11 - Low Air Pressure Warning

question: How does the air brake system's stop light switch work?
choice_a: It is mechanically linked directly to the parking brake lever
choice_b: It only activates when the ABS system engages
choice_c: It is triggered by the governor reaching cut-out pressure
choice_d: It is an electric switch that works by air pressure and turns on the brake lights when the air brakes are applied
explanation: The manual states the air brake system uses an electric switch that works by air pressure to turn on the brake lights when the driver applies the air brakes.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.12 - Stop Light Switch

topic: Front brake limiting valve - vehicle age
question: According to the manual, a front brake limiting valve with a cab control (marked "normal" and "slippery") is found on what vehicles?
explanation: The manual states that some older vehicles, made before 1975, have a front brake limiting valve and a control in the cab marked "normal" and "slippery."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.13 - Front Brake Limiting Valve

topic: Front brake limiting valve - slippery position
question: On a front brake limiting valve, what does putting the control in the "slippery" position do?
choice_a: It doubles air pressure to the front brakes
choice_b: It cuts the normal air pressure to the front brakes by half
choice_c: It disables the rear brakes entirely
choice_d: It immediately engages the spring brakes
explanation: The manual states that in the "slippery" position, the limiting valve cuts the normal air pressure to the front brakes by half, though this actually reduces the vehicle's stopping power.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.13 - Front Brake Limiting Valve

question: According to the manual, what have tests shown about front wheel skids caused by braking?
choice_a: They are common even on dry pavement
choice_b: They should always be prevented using a limiting valve on wet roads
choice_c: Front wheel skids from braking are not likely, even on ice
choice_d: Front brakes provide no meaningful stopping power
explanation: The manual states that tests have shown front wheel skids from braking are not likely even on ice, and front wheel braking is good under all conditions.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.13 - Front Brake Limiting Valve

question: Automatic front wheel limiting valves reduce air to the front brakes except when the brakes are applied very hard, at what application pressure or more?
explanation: The manual states automatic front wheel limiting valves reduce air to the front brakes except when the brakes are put on very hard, at 60 psi or more application pressure, and cannot be controlled by the driver.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.13 - Front Brake Limiting Valve

question: Why must emergency and parking brakes on trucks, truck tractors, and buses be held on by mechanical force rather than air pressure?
choice_a: Because air pressure can eventually leak away
choice_b: Because mechanical force applies the brakes faster
choice_c: Because air pressure would damage the brake drums
choice_d: Because it is only required on buses, not trucks
explanation: The manual explains that emergency and parking brakes must be held on by mechanical force because air pressure can eventually leak away; spring brakes are usually used to meet this need.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.14 - Spring Brakes

question: Tractor and straight truck spring brakes will come fully on when air pressure drops to what range?
explanation: The manual states that tractor and straight truck spring brakes will come fully on when air pressure drops to a range of 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.14 - Spring Brakes

question: Within the 20-45 psi range where spring brakes come fully on, what does the manual say is the typical range?
explanation: The manual states spring brakes come fully on in a range of 20 to 45 psi, typically 20 to 30 psi.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.14 - Spring Brakes

topic: Response to low air pressure warning
question: What does the manual instruct when the low air pressure warning light and buzzer first come on?
choice_a: Continue driving until the spring brakes engage automatically
choice_b: Increase speed to reach the nearest repair shop quickly
choice_c: Ignore it if only the buzzer, not the light, is sounding
choice_d: Bring the vehicle to a safe stop right away, while you can still control the brakes
explanation: The manual warns not to wait for the brakes to come on automatically; when the low air pressure warning first activates, bring the vehicle to a safe stop right away while you can still control the brakes.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.14 - Spring Brakes

question: In newer vehicles with air brakes, what does the manual say the parking brake control looks like?
explanation: The manual states that in newer vehicles, you put on the parking brakes using a diamond-shaped, yellow, push-pull control knob (older vehicles may use a lever or round knob of another shape).
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.15 - Parking Brake Controls

question: What is a modulating control valve, as described in the manual?
choice_a: A valve that automatically drains water and oil from the air tanks
choice_b: A spring-loaded dash board control handle that lets the driver apply the spring brakes gradually
choice_c: A device used to test the ABS malfunction lamp
choice_d: A valve that cuts front brake pressure by half on slippery roads
explanation: The manual describes the modulating control valve as a dash-mounted, spring-loaded control handle that lets the driver apply the spring brakes gradually if service brakes fail.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.15 - Parking Brake Controls

topic: Dual parking control valves - separate air tank
question: On vehicles such as buses equipped with dual parking control valves and a separate air tank, what is that separate tank used for?
choice_b: To inflate tires in a roadside emergency
choice_c: To operate the wig wag warning device
choice_d: To temporarily release the spring brakes so the driver can move the vehicle in an emergency after main air pressure is lost
explanation: The manual explains that when main air pressure is lost and spring brakes come on, some vehicles have a separate air tank that lets the driver push in a control to release the spring brakes temporarily and move the vehicle.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.15 - Parking Brake Controls (Dual Parking Control Valves)

question: According to the manual, truck tractors with air brakes built on or after what date are required to be equipped with antilock brakes (ABS)?
explanation: The manual states truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 are required to be equipped with ABS.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.16 - Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

topic: ABS requirement - other air brake vehicles
question: Other air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies), not truck tractors, are required to have ABS if built on or after what date?
explanation: The manual states other air brake vehicles - trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies - built on or after March 1, 1998, are required to be equipped with ABS.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.16 - Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: What color are the ABS malfunction lamps described in the manual?
explanation: The manual states vehicles with ABS have yellow malfunction lamps to tell the driver if something isn't working.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.16 - Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Where are yellow ABS malfunction lamps located on trailers, according to the manual?
choice_a: On the dashboard, visible to the driver
choice_b: On the right side, rear corner only
choice_c: On the left side, either the front or rear corner
choice_d: Inside the cab near the parking brake control
explanation: The manual states trailers will have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the left side, either the front or rear corner.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.16 - Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: According to the manual, does ABS necessarily shorten your stopping distance?
choice_a: Yes, it always significantly shortens stopping distance
choice_b: Yes, but only on wet pavement
choice_c: No, it has no effect on vehicle control
choice_d: Not necessarily, but it helps you keep the vehicle under control during hard braking
explanation: The manual states ABS does not necessarily shorten your stopping distance, but it does help you keep the vehicle under control during hard braking.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.16 - Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

topic: ABS malfunction lamp - start-up bulb check
question: On newer vehicles, what happens to the ABS malfunction lamp at start-up?
choice_a: It comes on for a bulb check, then goes out quickly
choice_b: It stays on for the entire trip regardless of ABS function
choice_c: It flashes continuously until the vehicle reaches 55 mph
choice_d: It never illuminates unless there is a malfunction
explanation: The manual states that on newer vehicles, the malfunction lamp comes on at start-up for a bulb check, and then goes out quickly; on older systems it could stay on until driving over five mph.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.1.16 - Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: In a dual air brake system, what are the two separate systems called?
choice_a: The manual system and the automatic system
choice_b: The primary system and the secondary system
choice_c: The service system and the emergency system
choice_d: The compressor system and the reservoir system
explanation: The manual states one system is called the "primary" system and the other is called the "secondary" system, and both supply air to the trailer if there is one.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.2 - Dual Air Brake

topic: Dual air system - minimum pressure before driving
question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, you should allow time for the compressor to build up a minimum pressure of how much in both the primary and secondary systems?
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to allow time for the air compressor to build up a minimum of 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.2 - Dual Air Brake

question: In a dual air brake system, at what pressure should the low air pressure warning light and buzzer shut off?
choice_d: At a manufacturer-set value that must be greater than 60 psi
explanation: The manual states the warning light and buzzer should shut off when air pressure in both systems rises to a value set by the manufacturer, and this value must be greater than 60 psi.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.2 - Dual Air Brake

question: What is the first step described for checking slack adjusters on s-cam brakes?
choice_a: Park on level ground and chock the wheels to prevent the vehicle from moving
choice_b: Apply the parking brakes fully before pulling on the adjuster
explanation: The manual instructs to park on level ground and chock the wheels, then release the parking brakes so the slack adjusters can be moved and pulled on.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.2 - Walk-around Inspection (Slack Adjusters)

question: When checking a slack adjuster by pulling hard on it, how much movement (where the push rod attaches) indicates it probably needs adjustment?
explanation: The manual states if a slack adjuster moves more than about one inch where the push rod attaches, it probably needs adjustment.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.2 - Walk-around Inspection (Slack Adjusters)

question: According to the manual, all vehicles built since what year have automatic slack adjusters?
explanation: The manual states all vehicles built since 1994 have automatic slack adjustors, though they must still be checked even though they adjust during full brake applications.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.2 - Walk-around Inspection (Slack Adjusters)

topic: Manual adjustment of automatic slack adjusters
question: Why does the manual describe manually adjusting an automatic slack adjuster as dangerous?
choice_b: It automatically triggers the safety valve to open
choice_c: It disables the ABS system permanently
choice_d: It may give the driver a false sense of security because it usually masks, rather than fixes, the underlying mechanical adjustment problem
explanation: The manual states manual adjustment of automatic slack adjusters is dangerous because it may give a false sense of security regarding braking effectiveness, since it generally masks rather than fixes the problem.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.2 - Walk-around Inspection (Slack Adjusters)

question: According to the manual, brake drums (or discs) must not have cracks longer than what?
choice_a: One half the width of the friction area
choice_b: One quarter the width of the friction area
choice_c: The full width of the friction area
choice_d: Any crack at all, regardless of length, is disqualifying only if visible without tools
explanation: The manual states brake drums or discs must not have cracks longer than one half the width of the friction area.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.2 - Walk-around Inspection (Brake Drums, Linings, and Hoses)

topic: Air compressor drive belt inspection step
question: During which step of the vehicle inspection should you check the air compressor drive belt, if the compressor is belt-driven?
explanation: The manual places checking the air compressor drive belt (if belt-driven) under Step 2, Engine Compartment Checks, of the seven-step inspection procedure.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.1 - Engine Compartment Checks

question: How does the manual describe testing the low pressure warning signal?
choice_a: Drive at highway speed and watch for the light to flicker
choice_b: Fully charge the tanks and open the safety valve manually
choice_c: Shut off the engine with enough air pressure that the signal is off, turn on electrical power, and step on and off the brake pedal until the warning comes on before pressure drops below 60 psi
choice_d: Disconnect the compressor and let pressure drop to zero
explanation: The manual instructs shutting off the engine with sufficient air pressure that the warning is not on, turning on electrical power, and stepping on and off the brake pedal to reduce tank pressure; the signal must come on before pressure drops below 60 psi.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check (Test Low Pressure Warning Signal)

question: When checking that spring brakes come on automatically, at what pressure range (per manufacturer specification) should the tractor protection valve and/or parking brake valve pop out?
explanation: The manual states the tractor protection valve and parking brake valve should close (pop out) when air pressure falls to the manufacturer's specification of 20 to 45 psi, causing the spring brakes to come on.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check (Check That Spring Brakes Come On Automatically)

topic: Air pressure buildup rate - dual air systems
question: In dual air systems, with the engine at operating rpm, the manual says pressure should build up from what range within 45 seconds?
explanation: The manual states that in dual air systems, pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds when the engine is at operating rpm.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check (Check Rate of Air Pressure Buildup)

topic: Air pressure buildup rate - single air systems (pre-1975)
question: For single air systems (pre-1975), the manual gives a typical buildup requirement of pressure rising from 50 to 90 psi within what time, at what idle speed?
choice_b: Within 3 minutes with the engine idling at 600-900 rpm
explanation: The manual states single air systems (pre-1975) typically require pressure build-up from 50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes with the engine at an idle speed of 600-900 rpm.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check (Check Rate of Air Pressure Buildup)

question: When testing air leakage rate on a fully-charged single vehicle (typically 125 psi) with the engine off and parking brake released, the loss rate should be less than what?
explanation: The manual states the air leakage loss rate should be less than two psi in one minute for single vehicles.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check (Test Air Leakage Rate)

question: For combination vehicles, the manual states the air leakage loss rate should be less than what, under the same test conditions?
explanation: The manual states the loss rate should be less than three psi in one minute for combination vehicles during the air leakage rate test.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check (Test Air Leakage Rate)

question: When checking that spring brakes come on automatically at the required pressure, the manual describes building air pressure up to governor cutoff, which range?
explanation: The manual states to build the air pressure up to governor cutoff (120-140 psi), then shut off the engine, release the parking brake and tractor protection valve, and fully apply the foot brake for one minute to check the drop.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check (Check That Spring Brakes Come On Automatically)

topic: One-minute foot brake hold test - single vehicle
question: During the one-minute foot-brake-hold test (after building pressure to governor cutoff), how much can the air pressure drop for a single vehicle before it indicates too much air loss?
explanation: The manual states that if the air pressure falls more than three psi in one minute for single vehicles, the air loss rate is too much and must be fixed.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check (Check That Spring Brakes Come On Automatically)

topic: One-minute foot brake hold test - combination vehicle
question: For a combination vehicle during the same one-minute foot-brake-hold test, how much air pressure drop indicates too much air loss?
explanation: The manual states that for combination vehicles, if the air pressure falls more than four psi in one minute, the air loss rate is too much.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check (Check That Spring Brakes Come On Automatically)

question: When checking the air compressor governor cut-in and cut-out pressures during the final inspection, at approximately what pressures should pumping start and stop?
choice_a: Start at about 125 psi and stop at about 150 psi
choice_b: Start at about 60 psi and stop at about 100 psi
choice_c: Start at about 20 psi and stop at about 45 psi
choice_d: Start at about 100 psi and stop at about 125 psi
explanation: The manual states pumping by the air compressor should start at about 100 psi (cut-in) and stop at about 125 psi (cut-out), checking manufacturer specifications.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check (Check Air Compressor Governor Cut-in and Cut-out Pressures)

question: How does the manual describe testing the parking brake during the final air brake check?
choice_a: Stop the vehicle, put the parking brake on, and gently pull against it in a low gear
choice_b: Drive at 5 mph and apply the parking brake suddenly
choice_c: Release the parking brake and coast down a hill
choice_d: Apply the parking brake while accelerating in a high gear
explanation: The manual instructs to stop the vehicle, put the parking brake on, and gently pull against it in a low gear to test that the parking brake will hold.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check (Test Parking Brake)

question: How does the manual describe testing the service brakes during the final air brake check?
choice_a: Drive at 55 mph and brake as hard as possible
choice_b: Move the vehicle forward slowly, about five mph, and apply the brakes firmly, noting any pulling, unusual feel, or delayed stopping action
choice_c: Test the brakes only while the parking brake remains applied
choice_d: Accelerate to governor cut-out pressure before applying the brakes
explanation: The manual instructs waiting for normal air pressure, releasing the parking brake, moving the vehicle forward slowly (about five mph), and applying the brakes firmly, noting any pulling, unusual feel, or delayed stopping action.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.3.3 - Final Air Brake Check (Test Service Brakes)

question: According to the manual, what four factors together make up the total stopping distance for a vehicle with air brakes?
choice_a: Reaction distance, braking distance, and tire wear (three factors)
choice_b: Perception distance, braking distance, and governor lag (three factors)
choice_c: Perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance
choice_d: Brake lag distance, tire distance, and engine braking distance (three factors)
explanation: The manual gives the formula: Perception Distance + Reaction Distance + Brake Lag Distance + Braking Distance = Total Stopping Distance.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.4.4 - Stopping Distance

question: According to the manual, about how many additional feet does air brake lag distance add at 55 mph on dry pavement?
explanation: The manual states the air brake lag distance at 55 mph on dry pavement adds about 32 feet, since it takes one half second or more for air to flow through the lines to the brakes.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.4.4 - Stopping Distance

question: According to the manual, for an average driver under good traction and brake conditions at 55 mph, the total stopping distance for a vehicle with air brakes is over how many feet?
explanation: The manual states that at 55 mph for an average driver under good traction and brake conditions, the total stopping distance for a vehicle with air brakes is over 450 feet.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 5.4.4 - Stopping Distance
